answer: Every honest vote on the wharf starts as a timber beam. The agent buys the beam by locking $20 escrow to its key, then crosses a nine-span toll bridge: five minutes of signed liveness per span, same key all the way. The wharf warden knocks the timber at a random span: real hardware rings unique, cloned rigs ring identical, and a matched pair loses beam, escrow, and six epochs. Forging 10,000 votes costs 7,500 hours plus $200,000 in escrows, hauling a forest across the bridge plank by plank while the warden listens: one hollow ring, and the whole load goes into the drink.
